name: Ibn Saud
role: King of Saudi Arabia from 1932 to 1953
contribution: A Najdi war leader, statesman, and religious leader who became the founder and first King of Saudi Arabia, reigning from 23 September 1932 until his death in 1953.
legacy: This person reconquered Riyadh in 1902, starting three decades of conquests that made him the ruler of nearly all of central and north Arabia

checks.lead: Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman bin Faisal Al Saud (Arabic: عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ بْنِ فَيْصَلٍ آلِ سُعُود, romanized: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Fayṣal Āl Saʿūd; 15 January 1876 – 9 November 1953), known in the Western world as Ibn Saud (Arabic: ابن سعود; Ibn Suʿūd), and known with his kunya Abu Turki (Arabic: أَبُو تُرْكِي), was a Najdi war leader, statesman, and religious leader who became the founder and first King of Saudi Arabia, reigning from 23 September 1932 until his death in 1953. He had ruled parts of the kingdom since 1902, having previously been Emir, Sultan, King of Nejd, and King of Hejaz.
